meta.title: Mobile View: Responsive Website Tester & Device Emulator for Chrome
meta.description: Free Chrome extension to test responsive sites on real iPhone, Android, iPad, Mac and Apple Watch frames side by side, with synced scrolling. Works on localhost.
meta.ogTitle: Mobile View: see your site on every screen at once
meta.ogImageAlt: Mobile View showing one page on iPhone, a foldable, a MacBook and an Apple Watch side by side

hero.title: See your site on every screen at once.
hero.lede: A free Chrome extension that shows any page, even localhost, on real phones, foldables, tablets, laptops and watches. Side by side, in sync.

demo.label: Live demo
demo.badge: Live. Scroll or tap any screen.

tour.workspaceText: Pick any four of {count} real devices and see your page on all of them at once.
tour.workspaceAlt: Mobile View workspace showing a page on iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone Duo folded, MacBook Pro 14 and Apple Watch side by side
tour.syncText: Scrolling, clicks and navigation stay in sync across devices.
tour.syncAlt: Four devices scrolled to the same point of a page with scroll and navigation sync turned on
tour.allText: Open a whole category at once. Here, 16 of 37 iPhones, from the iPhone 5 to the iPhone 15 Pro.
tour.allAlt: All devices view showing two rows of iPhones, from iPhone 5 and iPhone SE to iPhone 15 Pro, each loading the same page
tour.designText: Drop your mockup next to the live page on any device. Side by side or overlaid, every gap between design and build is easy to spot.
tour.designItem1Detail: Live: "Make room for your best work." Design: "Room for your best work."
tour.designItem2Detail: Live: dark, square corners. Design: teal pill.
tour.designAlt: Compare with design: the live page on iPhone 18 Pro beside the design image, with a different headline and button style
tour.fixTitle: Mark the bug. Copy the fix.
tour.fixText: Draw on a screenshot, then copy a ready prompt for your AI coding tool. Nothing leaves your machine.
tour.fixAlt: Annotation editor with an arrow and box marking a heading on the iPhone, next to the fix prompt panel listing the affected devices

privacy.title: Private by design.
privacy.item3: Your pages stay in your browser

faq.title: Questions.
faq.a1: Yes. Free and open source under the MIT license, with no account.
faq.a2: Yes. Open your local page in Chrome, then open Mobile View. Nothing leaves your computer.
faq.q3: How is it different from DevTools device mode?
faq.a3: DevTools shows one viewport at a time. Mobile View shows four real devices side by side, kept in sync.
faq.a4: Some sites block being shown inside another page. Mobile View tells you and offers to open them in a tab.
faq.q5: Does the fix prompt upload my code?
faq.a5: No. It is written on your machine for you to paste into your own coding tool.

cta.title: Try it on your own site.
cta.text: Free. No account. Works on localhost.
